items.title: [Bug]: Identity entry in packed_modules_mapping silently disables layer_quant_config (Quark)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### The bug

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` — a mapping of a module to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]` — silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config` instead, so a mixed-precision checkpoint gets built with
the wrong scheme and fails at weight load with a shape mismatch.

In `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py`, both lookup paths treat
`shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information available":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
shard_name = layer_name.replace(proj_name, shard_proj_name)
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None                      # <-- identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:
    config = fallback_config           # <-- identity entry -> global scheme
```

For a genuine fusion (`fused_qkv_a_proj` -> `[q_a_proj, kv_a_proj_with_mqa]`) that is right: the
shard names differ, and the entries are looked up individually. For an identity entry the
substitution is a no-op, and the code concludes there is nothing to look up — even though
`layer_quant_config` may contain the layer under its own name.

### Who this affects

Identity entries are an established pattern in-tree, not a mistake by checkpoint authors:

```
vllm/model_executor/models/plamo3.py:375     "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],
vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py:1769   "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],
vllm/model_executor/models/molmo.py:1313     "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],  # language model
```

Any Quark checkpoint that uses `layer_quant_config` to give one of these modules a different
scheme than the global one is affected. It is silent until load: no warning, no log line, just the
global scheme applied where a per-layer scheme was specified.

### Reproduction

GLM-5.3-Flash, Quark MXFP4 checkpoint with `layer_quant_config` marking the dense MLPs

items.title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL issues up to ~112k KV descriptors per rank-transfer, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**.

The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's.

Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below.

### Measurements

GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion.

| Transport | Descriptors / transfer | Post mean | Total mean | Movement remainder | Payload / remainder | Post share |

| MNNVL `cuda_ipc` | 112,092 | **455.9 ms** | 800.8 ms | 345.0 ms | 14.16 GB/s | **56.9%** |
| Native IB `rc_x`, 4 rails | 119,984 | 24.4 ms | 350.8 ms | 326.4 ms | 15.11 GB/s | 7.0% |

Amortized submission cost per descriptor: `rc_x` IB **0.204 µs**, `rc_x` RoCE **0.352 µs**, `cuda_ipc` **4.067 µs**.

Closes #38006. Enables sparse MLA models (GLM-5, DeepSeek-V3.2) on SM80 (A100/A800) and SM121 (GB10/DGX Spark), where DeepGEMM / FlashMLA-Sparse / FlashInfer-MLA-Sparse are unavailable.

1. **Dispatch guard.** `is_deep_gemm_supported()` (SM90+ check) replaces `has_deep_gemm()` in `sparse_attn_indexer.py` / `indexer.py`. Stops DeepGEMM kernels from being invoked on SM80/SM121.

Prefill takes bf16 q/k (pre-decoded from FP8 in the Python wrapper) and feeds a straight `tl.dot`; paged decode keeps a 256-entry bf16 LUT for in-kernel FP8 decode. items.title: [ROCm] Support unlimited sequence lengths via multi-pass reduction
items.bodyExcerpt:
At present, on ROCm for certain models including GLM-4.7, vLLM has a choice between two attention implementations from vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py. One is a very slow reference Triton kernel and the other is a  hand-coded op. The custom op only supports context length up to 131072 tokens, which means that, unless vLLM is set to eager mode, it'll only be used if max_seq_len is <131072 (otherwise, since actual context length is unknown at graph capture time, it defaults to Triton for all context lengths).

This patch drops the 131072 token cap and adds a multi-pass mode to support  unlimited max_seq_len. It also adds unit tests to cover this scenario.

This results in a drastic increase in token generation throughput on ROCm for GLM-4.7 for max_seq_len>131072.

Throughput, token/s, 4x MI325x (2026/Sep/09)
Context | max_model_len | PR - throughput | Baseline - throughput
-- | -- | -- | --
65536 | 75536 | 55.05 | 55.08
100000 | 110000 | 50.21 | 50.09
150000 | 160000 | 42.66 | 0.47

The PR also includes the fix for correctness issue reported by @davetha below.

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.

## Purpose

Enables GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) end-to-end on `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`
for gfx942/gfx950. Routing is opt-in via `--model-class-overrides`; the registry entry
is unchanged, so the default path for GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 is untouched. 

The following issues were also fixed as a result of this overall enablement since it surfaced dormant bugs from a prior deepseek_v32 porting work:

- **`launch_pdl` forwarded to a Triton runtime that doesn't accept it** — the shared
  `common/kernels.py` passed this CUDA-only kwarg unconditionally; ROCm's Triton rejects
  it by name even when `False`, so the engine died at startup with `KeyError`. Now passed
  only when the platform actually supports PDL.

- **fp4 bmm invoked with mismatched positional args** — the output tensor landed in the
  kernel's `dtype` slot (`Expected 'Optional[int]' for 'dtype' but found Tensor`). Routed
  through the existing `rocm_aiter_ops.batched_gemm_a16wfp4` wrapper rather than calling
  aiter directly, so the argument contract lives in one place.

items.title: [ROCm][Model][AMD][Performance]: Added AITER fusion on top of the existing TRITON fusion path for GLM-5.2-MXFP4 through deepseek_v32
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Adds an AITER-backed fusion path for the ROCm `deepseek_v32` (DeepSeek Sparse
Attention) forward, used by both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2. The existing
shared-Triton fusion path is untouched and remains the default; the AITER path
is selected at runtime per fusion via opt-in env flags, so behaviour on ROCm is
unchanged unless a flag is set.

This PR is stacked on top of: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51915, so needs enablement to land first before this fusion add-on.

### Fusions added

**1. MLA dual RMSNorm** 
Fuses the q and kv-a RMSNorms into one AITER call
(`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_out`). An out-variant was added so the norms write
model-owned buffers rather than allocating per layer, which lets the call be
hoisted out of the eager region and captured by cudagraph. Also wires the
per-token-quant variant for the quantized case.

**2. Fused QK RoPE + concat + MLA cache write** 
`rocm_aiter_fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` replaces the separate RoPE,
concat and KV-cache-write steps on the MLA path. The uint8 KV cache allocated by
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is viewed as `float8_e4m3fn` before the call, since the
AITER op rejects the raw uint8 buffer.

**3. Fused indexer QK RoPE + fp8 quant + cache write**
`rocm_aiter_indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` fuses the lightning-indexer key
LayerNorm, RoPE, fp8 quantization, and cache write into one call for the 21
indexer layers.

**4. Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm**
Uses AITER's custom all-reduce with an in-kernel RMSNorm. Gated on custom-AR
eligibility (`should_custom_ar`) because the op asserts the kernel ran, and
oversized batches must fall back to the standard path — this is the check the
torch.compile pass performs at compile time and which an inline call has to do
itself.

**5. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR`** exposes AITER's custom all-reduce
independently of the fused variant.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54641 — reported and diagnosed by @stefanskiasan.

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` (a module mapped to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]`) silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config`, so a mixed-precision Quark checkpoint is built with the
wrong scheme and only fails later, at weight load, with a shape mismatch.

Both lookup paths in `QuarkConfig` treat `shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None              # identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:

```

For such an entry the shard name *is* the layer name, so the lookup should resolve it rather than

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
`compute_block_transfer_offsets` in the MoRI-IO KV connector raised `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` whenever the producer's local block count exceeded the consumer's. Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** with `block_size=1`, the prefill (producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead slots that the decode (consumer) side does not allocate, so `local` exceeds `remote` by exactly the spec-token count (e.g. **8003 vs 8000** at n=3). This crashed the first prefill→decode KV write and made MTP unusable over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation.

## Fix
Block order is positional (`block_size=1`), so the prompt KV is the prefix and the extra local blocks are empty lookahead scratch. Clamp `local_block_ids` to `local[:len(remote)]` and transfer only the prompt prefix — symmetric with the existing shorter-local handling already documented in the same function.

## Tests

- Replaces the now-obsolete longer-local *raise* test with **clamp-to-prompt-prefix** tests for both the interleaved (`transfers_per_block=1`) and separated split-KV (`transfers_per_block=2`) layouts, asserting the result is identical to transferring `local[:len(remote)]`.
- Adds a shorter-local regression guard (pre-existing READ-mode partial transfer unchanged).

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Warm up the Triton fused MoE GEMMs
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_moe_kernel` is the expert GEMM whenever DeepGEMM declines the shape. The
dominant case is the `N <= 512` early-out in `_valid_deep_gemm`
(`experts/deep_gemm_moe.py`): a model with a small `moe_intermediate_size`
crosses that threshold as soon as TP is high enough, and from then on never uses
DeepGEMM. GLM-5.2-FP8 at TP=8 gives `w2 = (256, 6144, 256)`, i.e. `N=256`, so its
whole MoE stack runs on Triton for every request.

Nothing in the startup path compiles that kernel for the variants real batches
select. Two things vary with the token count `M`:

1. the tile config, chosen by `try_get_optimal_moe_config` from a tuned config
   file or `get_default_config`;
2. the 16-divisibility of `EM` and `num_valid_tokens`, which Triton attaches as
   a `tt.divisibility` attribute and keys separately.

Profiling and CUDA graph capture only reach a few of these combinations, so the
first request landing on an uncompiled one JIT-compiles mid-serving. Measured on
GLM-5.2-FP8 at TP=8, main compiles 4 distinct variants per rank during
inference (32 events across 8 ranks). With `--jit-monitor-mode=error` that is a
hard failure; with the default `warn` it is a latency spike.

## Changes

- New `vllm/model_executor/warmup/triton_moe_warmup.py`: walks the `M` values
  that can select a distinct tile config, pairs each with a neighbour that flips
  the 16-divisibility of `num_valid_tokens` so both variants compile, and runs
  the expert GEMMs through `TritonExperts.apply` once per value.
- Called from `kernel_warmup` inside the existing `enable_jit_warmup` block.

Design notes:

- Warmup drives `TritonExperts.apply` rather than reconstructing the ~30 kernel
  arguments. `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` derives the strides, `EM`,
  `SWAP_AB` and the effective `BLOCK_SIZE_K` from the tensors it is handed, so
  going through the real path is the only way to guarantee the compiled key

Three small, independent decode hot-path cleanups found while profiling GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, FP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`):

1. **KDA decode: read token-strided q/k/v/beta in `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`.** The decode path hands the recurrent kernel column slices of the merged `q|k|v` conv output and of the fused `qkvbfg_a` projection (beta); `fused_recurrent_kda` made each contiguous, i.e. 4 copy kernels per KDA layer per step (34 layers; ~11 us/layer at 64 requests, ~0.4 ms/step). The Triton kernel now takes explicit token strides; contiguous callers are unchanged. The stride check is pure integer arithmetic (no views) because the KDA forward is a CUDA-graph break and runs eagerly.
2. **MLA: write the absorbed MQA query token-major and skip the empty RoPE concat.** Without head padding the W_UK bmm now writes into a `(B, N, L)` buffer through a transposed `out` view (verified: one GEMM kernel, no copy, identical result). 3. **Glm5NextMoE: do not compute the router logits twice.** `MoERunner` holds the gate (passed via `FusedMoEFactory`) and recomputes the logits (`moe_runner.py:897`), so the gate GEMM in `Glm5NextMoE.forward` was wasted (two bf16->fp32 GEMMs + reductions per MoE layer). Follows `DeepseekV2MoE` and passes a placeholder.

items.title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Use FlashKDA for KDA chunked prefill (1.7-3.8x faster than the Triton chunk path)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Use **FlashKDA** (`vllm._flashkda_C`, already built and used by Kimi-K3) for GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA chunked prefill instead of the ~15-kernel Triton `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` path.

FlashKDA implements the same bounded-gate KDA recurrence GLM-5.3-Flash uses (`lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (g + dt_bias))`, in-kernel q/k l2norm, raw beta logits), so it is a drop-in. On GB300 per KDA layer (H=16/rank, D=128, `bench/flashkda_vs_chunk.py`):

| shape | Triton chunk path | FlashKDA |
|---|---|---|
| 8 x 2048 tokens | 183 us | 49 us |
| 4 x 8192 | 555 us | 146 us |
| 1 x 16384 | 1371 us | 787 us |

Selection: automatic when supported (SM90/SM10x/SM12x, bf16, head_dim 128, bounded gate); `additional_config.kda_prefill_backend = triton` keeps the old path (`flashkda` forces it). The output is written straight into the layer buffer (no merge copy) and the pre-sigmoid beta cast is not needed on this path. Spec-decode tokens themselves keep the Triton recurrent kernel (`num_accepted_tokens` rollback); in a step that carries both, FlashKDA runs the prefill segment into a workspace buffer and the outputs are scattered back by `non_spec_token_indx` / `spec_token_indx` (same scheme as the Kimi-K3 KDA layer; the merge writes straight into `core_attn_out`).

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Bound kpool prefill tail-seed stores by NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS
items.bodyExcerpt:
Prefill `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` stores into `tail[blk]` using `blk = tslot // kpool`. After prefix-cache churn, `tslot` can carry a **main-KV-magnitude physical id** while the tail tensor is a 1-block-per-request ring (`n_tail` << physical id). Decode already skipped `block >= n_tail`; seed did not.

## Measured (gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4)

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56037 **Crash D** (2026-09-07).

- Dying step: chunked prefill, computed=211200, scheduled=2338 (`2338 % 4 == 2` so the last chunk must seed the tail ring), `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}`, `new_block_ids` around 3535–3578.
- `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3` on the dying image, GPU 0 only:

```
hipModuleGetFunction(..., _kpool_tail_seed_kernel)
ShaderName : _kpool_tail_seed_kernel
Memory Fault Error
Memory access fault by GPU node-2
```

Same probe with `if blk >= NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS: return` does not fault.

## This PR

Pass `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS = tail_kv_cache.shape[0]` into the prefill seed kernel (AMD + NVIDIA copies) and return before the store when `blk` is out of range.

**Out of scope:** mixed-length MTP decode (Crash C) and equal-length short MTP decode (Crash E) in #56037. Those are separate paths; do not close #56037 on this PR alone.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Poolside: stray arg_key tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`PoolsideV1ToolParser.func_arg_regex` captures the argument key with a plain
`.*?`:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>", re.DOTALL
)
```

A non-greedy `.*?` guarantees only the *shortest match consistent with the
rest of the pattern*, not that it stops at the first literal `</arg_key>`.
If `\s*<arg_value>` fails to match right after that first occurrence, the
engine backtracks and lets `.*?` cross the boundary to reach a *later*
`</arg_key>`, silently absorbing a stray `<arg_key>`/`</arg_key>` tag into
the parsed key.

This is the identical defect class and identical fix shape as the GLM-4.7
leak fixed in #54971 (reviewer Manny7717 flagged this exact call site in
that PR's review, at `vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py:82`).
The fix bounds the key to runs of non-`<` text, so the capture group can
never cross its own delimiter:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>([^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
    r"<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

This file uses the third-party `regex` module (`import regex as re`), not
stdlib `re` — `regex` has always supported possessive quantifiers (`*+`)
regardless of interpreter version, so (unlike a stdlib-`re` site) no
non-possessive fallback is needed here. The repo's `requires-python` floor
is `>=3.10,<3.15`; the dev venv used for testing runs 3.13.15, and a
20,000-case randomized differential check (see Test Result) against the
old pattern found no divergence on well-formed input and no leaked `<` in
malformed input.

Searched open PRs against `poolside`/`arg_key`/`tool_parsers` before
starting. The only overlapping PR is #54678
("[Bugfix][Security] Fix catastrophic backtracking in the poolside_v1 and
dots tool-call regexes"), which is **not** a duplicate of this fix: it
targets a different defect class (ReDoS/timing) in the *same file*'s

items.title: [Bugfix] Recover hybrid invalid-block KV load failures instead of crashing EngineCore
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Scheduler._update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` unpacks a single block-id list:

```python
(req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
```

For a hybrid (multi-group) model attached to a KV connector, `get_block_ids` returns one list per KV cache group, so the first failed remote chunk load kills EngineCore with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1, got N)` — observed live on GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 (6 groups) with dfkv/Mooncake-style stores; the same crash reproduces with any KV connector on a hybrid model.

Even without the crash, the single-group recovery semantics (truncate `num_computed_tokens` at the first failed block and resume) are unsound for hybrid models: state groups (mamba) depend on the full-attention group's boundary state, so resuming one group at a partial prefix while another group failed produces silently inconsistent KV.

This PR makes hybrid requests replay from zero with every participating group's prefix hashes invalidated:

- Coverage per group uses the engine's own outer-spec rule (AttentionSpec scaled by DCP; other specs unscaled) over groups that participate in prefix caching, considering only the possibly-externally-computed prefix.
- A failure in any group invalidates **every** participating group's cached block hashes via `kv_cache_manager.evict_blocks` (hash-only: receive buffers the connector still owns are not returned to the allocator).
- `recompute` policy (default): the request is marked `skip_reading_prefix_cache`, RUNNING requests are preempted through the normal `_preempt_request` path back into the waiting queue, and async `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests reset to zero so the existing finished-recv flow frees their groups.
- `fail` policy reports the affected requests and eviction set without touching recompute state; single-group requests keep the existing longest-valid-prefix and shared-block optimizations unchanged.

items.title: [WIP][Bugfix][HiSparse] Restore host mirror state before FULL CUDA graph replay
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix missing host KV writes during HiSparse FULL CUDA graph decode. Once GPU-resident pages are spilled, subsequent host fetches can read unwritten KV and corrupt generation without raising a serving error.

WIP, targeting `feat/hisparse-metrics` (#53782). This contains only the mirror-state correction, a guard against silently missing mirror metadata, and one regression test. CUDA graphs and async scheduling remain enabled.

## Reproduction and cause

We reproduced the issue with GLM-5.3 on two nodes / 16 H200 GPUs, EP16/TP1, using 1,024 concurrent fresh generations from 32 frozen long-reasoning math prompts. The configuration used FP8 KV, 4,096 hot rows, eager host mirroring, a 160 GiB host KV pool per rank, FULL decode graphs, async scheduling, and prefix caching disabled.

Output was initially readable. Resident KV reached capacity around 13.2k median context, and unrelated numeric-word garbling appeared around 13.9k as decoding began relying on host fetches. This happened without client errors or preemptions.

The connector clears per-batch mirror metadata at the beginning of each step. Eager execution rebuilds it in the Python attention path, but FULL graph replay bypasses that Python preparation. Newly written decode KV can therefore be left uncopied on the host. Later spills under eager mirroring trust the host copy, so the problem becomes visible only when those rows are fetched again.

The smaller regression isolates that missing write without a long benchmark: a dummy-weight sparse-MLA model performs FULL-graph decode with eager mirroring and async scheduling, then compares the final decoded token's host KV bytes with its resident GPU bytes. On the original implementation the host row is zero while the GPU row is nonzero.

## Change

- Prepare each HiSparse index-sharing group's per-batch mirror state after `kv_connector.pre_forward()` and before `run_fullgraph()` for real HiSparse batches.
- Raise an error when mirror completion has scheduled

## Bugs

1. Dense-MLP `gate_up_proj` resolves to the wrong quant scheme:
The class inherits `packed_modules_mapping = {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]}` from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration`. This identity mapping is correct for GLM-4.1V (whose checkpoint stores a pre-fused `gate_up_proj` tensor), but GLM-5.3-Flash stores gate/up as **separate** tensors (both the [Quark ](https://huggingface.co/amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4)and the [base](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) checkpoints). With the identity entry, `QuarkConfig` falls back to `global_quant_config` (MXFP4) instead of the per-layer block-FP8 in `layer_quant_config` and builds the layer as MXFP4 and mismatches the FP8 checkpoint tensor at load.


2. MLA projection scale name mismatch:
The MLA `q_a` / `kv_a` / `q_b` / `o` projections are dequantized on load by `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, which only recognized scales named `weight_scale_inv`. Quark checkpoints export `weight_scale`, so the scale fell through and the fused-qkv-a stacked mapping could not find its target.

## Changes (`vllm/model_executor/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`)

1. Override `packed_modules_mapping` on `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` so the  fused `gate_up_proj` expands to its real shard names `["gate_proj", "up_proj"]` (matching the `Glm4vMoeForConditionalGeneration` sibling / `glm4_moe` / `deepseek_v2`).
2. In `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, accept the Quark scale name:
   `is_scale = "weight_scale_inv" in name or name.endswith(".weight_scale")`.

## Related PRs and Issues:

Bug 1 was initially reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/
